title: Near-monochrome attention (speculative)
description: SPECULATIVE — not recommended over the current palette; default remains to keep the existing amber. Most conservative palette option: retires hue from attention states entirely. --color-accent-text becomes bright ink (#ffffff, i.e. brighter than --color-ink) and --color-amber-500 becomes a near-white ink tone; attention (PRÓXIMO, ABORDANDO/ahora, SALIENDO, the pulsing dot) is instead communicated purely via extra font-weight/brightness against the dark surface, not color. Simplest to reason about accessibility-wise since it removes color as an attention signal, at the cost of losing the amber's quick-glance scannability.

changes.intent: Remove hue as an attention signal; rely on brightness + weight only, for the most conservative/legible dark-mode option.
changes.detail: Dark theme values shown above (kiosk default). For light theme, --color-accent-text would become the darkest ink shade (near #000 or reuse --color-ink at full opacity) rather than a colored value, per the same 'brightness + weight, no hue' principle. Speculative and the most conservative of the three L options: default is to keep current amber (#ffd24e / #ffc107).

changes.intent: Compensate for the loss of hue contrast by adding weight, since brightness alone (without color) is a weaker attention cue.
changes.detail: These selectors are already font-weight 700-800 at baseline; this variation ensures they are pinned to the heavier 800 across the board so the mono accent-text token change reads clearly as 'emphasized' rather than just 'lighter grey'.
